content:
If you run physical shops and an online store, click and collect (customers buy or reserve online and pick up from a store) is often the quickest way to turn website visits into footfall. It is also simple to add on today's platforms. Ecommerce website development for a Pune retailer with one or more stores should treat it as a core feature with five parts: store pages and a store locator, per-store stock on product pages, a pickup option at checkout, clear "ready for collection" messages, and a handover process at the counter. Shopify and WooCommerce both have built-in local pickup features that cover most of this. The hard part is usually accurate store-level inventory and staff routines, not the code. This guide explains how to plan each piece, what the main platforms offer, and how pickup ties into Google search and Maps.

It is written for owners and managers of Indian retail businesses with physical stores (electronics, furniture, books and stationery, pharmacy and wellness where permitted, fashion, hardware, gifting, bakeries and food retail) who sell online or plan to.

## Why click and collect is worth building

For a retailer with stores, pickup solves several problems at once:

- **No delivery cost or wait for the customer.** People who live or work near a store can often collect the same day.
- **Lower delivery and return friction for you.** Collected orders avoid courier charges, and the customer can check the product at the counter.
- **Footfall.** A customer who comes in to collect may buy something else. That is the point of combining online and offline.
- **Trust.** Some customers are wary of buying expensive items from an unfamiliar website. Knowing they can collect from a real shop with a real address makes buying online feel safer.

It is not right for every business. If your stores carry very different stock from the website, if staff cannot keep store inventory accurate, or if most customers live far from any store, start with a store locator and "check availability" feature before offering full pickup.

## Part 1: Store pages and a store locator

Each physical store should have its own page on your website. That page does two jobs: it helps customers who want to visit, and it helps search engines understand that you have a local presence at that address.

### What each store page should include

- The store name as customers know it, for example "Kothrud store" or "FC Road store".
- Full address, an embedded map, landmark directions and parking information.
- Phone or WhatsApp number for that store, and opening hours including weekly offs and holiday changes.
- Pickup hours if they differ from opening hours, and where in the store to collect.
- Photographs of the shopfront and interior so customers recognise it.
- Services available at that store (pickup, returns, fitting, repairs).
- A link to browse products available at that store, if your platform supports it.

### The store locator

With two or three stores, a simple page listing them with maps is enough. With ten or more, a searchable locator (by area, pin code or "use my location") becomes worthwhile. Keep it fast: a locator that loads a heavy map script before showing any store list frustrates mobile users. Show a plain list first, then load the map.

### Local search details

Each store should have a matching, verified Google Business Profile, with name, address and phone identical to the store page, and the profile's website link pointing to that store's page rather than your homepage. Mark up each store page with LocalBusiness structured data describing that store. Our guides to [multi-location local SEO](/blog/local-seo-multi-location-businesses-india) and [LocalBusiness schema and NAP consistency](/blog/web-development-company-pune-localbusiness-schema-nap-opening-hours-2026) cover these details.

## Part 2: Store-level stock on product pages

Pickup only works if the website knows what is on each store's shelf. That is the decision that shapes everything else.

### Where store stock comes from

- **The ecommerce platform is the master.** Shopify, for example, tracks inventory per location. If your stores sell through Shopify POS, store sales reduce that store's stock automatically. This is the simplest setup.
- **A separate billing or POS system is the master.** Many Indian retailers already use a billing system in-store. Then you need an integration that sends stock levels from the POS to the website, ideally every few minutes and at least several times a day. The integration is the main development cost.
- **No reliable store stock.** If stores cannot keep counts accurate, offer "reserve and we will confirm" instead of instant "available for pickup", and say clearly that you will confirm by call or WhatsApp.

### Showing availability on the product page

The product page should show, near the price and the add-to-cart button:

- Whether the item can be picked up, and from which store, for example "Available for pickup today at Kothrud" or "In stock at 2 of 4 stores".
- A link or drawer to see all stores and change the preferred store.
- An honest message when stock is low or uncertain: "Last few at FC Road, we will confirm before you travel."

Remember the customer's chosen store so they do not need to select it on every page. Keep this light: per-store availability should load quickly and not block the rest of the page. Shopify notes that product-page pickup availability depends on your theme.

Build in a stock buffer. If the website shows the last unit as available and someone buys it in the store a minute later, the online customer arrives to find nothing. Many retailers hide pickup availability when store stock falls below a small threshold, such as two units.

## Part 3: The pickup option at checkout

At checkout, customers should choose between delivery and pickup clearly, early, and without having to enter a delivery address for pickup orders.

### What good checkout pickup looks like

- **Delivery or Pickup** as the first choice in the delivery step.
- A list of eligible stores with address, distance if location is shared, and expected ready time ("Usually ready in 2 hours", "Ready tomorrow after 11 am").
- Pickup instructions: what to bring (order number, the phone used at checkout, ID for high-value items) and how long you will hold the order.
- The pickup cost, if any, shown clearly. Most retailers make pickup free.
- No unnecessary address fields.

### What Shopify offers

Shopify's local pickup is set up per location under Settings, Shipping and delivery, Pickup in store, by enabling "Let customers pick up orders directly at this location". You set an expected pickup time that customers see, write pickup instructions that appear in the "Ready for pickup" email, and staff mark orders "Ready for pickup" and later "Picked up" from the order screen. By default pickup is offered only when the whole order is in stock at that location, and Shopify can create stock transfers from other locations. Customers only see pickup locations in their own country, and the chosen pickup location cannot be changed after checkout.

### What WooCommerce offers

WooCommerce's Checkout block includes a Local Pickup feature under WooCommerce, Settings, Shipping, Local Pickup. You enable it, rename the option if you like, add a price if you want to charge, and add one or more pickup locations with a name, address and pickup details such as collection hours. Customers then see "Ship" and "Pickup" choices in the delivery step and pick a location. WooCommerce documents some limits: all items in an order share one pickup location, and the block method ignores shipping zones (zone-based restrictions need the older "legacy" local pickup method). WooCommerce does not, out of the box, check per-store stock; for that you need an inventory plugin or custom development.

### Custom builds

On a custom platform, pickup is a fulfilment method that needs: a stores table, store-level stock, rules for which products are eligible (oversized furniture may be pickup-only from a warehouse; perishable items may need a collection window), slot or ready-time logic, and an order status flow. It costs more but fits unusual rules, such as pickup-only products or pickup from a partner location.

## Part 4: Order statuses and notifications

Customers need to know when to come. Without clear messages, people arrive too early, call the store repeatedly, or never come.

A simple status flow:

1. **Order placed:** confirmation with the store, address, expected ready time and what to bring.
2. **Ready for pickup:** sent only when the item is actually packed and set aside. Include store hours, a map link, the order number, and how long you will hold it.
3. **Reminder:** if not collected after a day or two.
4. **Picked up:** a short confirmation, which is also a good moment to ask for a review.
5. **Cancelled or not collected:** clear explanation and refund or next steps, following your published policy.

Email is the default on most platforms. WhatsApp is often more effective in India for "ready for pickup" and reminders, using approved utility templates through the WhatsApp Business API. Our article on [order updates over WhatsApp](/blog/whatsapp-order-updates-api-india) covers the setup. Note one Shopify detail: orders placed through the Facebook and Instagram channel do not send the "Ready for pickup" email, so those customers need to be contacted another way.

## Part 5: The counter process

The website can be perfect and the experience can still fail at the counter. Agree the routine with store staff before launch:

- **Who watches for new pickup orders**, how they are alerted (POS notification, email, a tablet), and how fast they must pick and pack.
- **Where orders are kept**, labelled with order number and customer name.
- **How the customer is verified:** order number plus phone number, or a one-time code shown in the confirmation. For expensive items, ask for ID and record it.
- **What happens if the item is missing or damaged** when picked: call the customer before they travel.
- **Holding period:** how many days you hold an uncollected order before cancelling, and whether the refund is automatic.
- **Payment at pickup:** if you allow "reserve now, pay at store", decide how to handle no-shows and ensure the stock is released.

Train staff with a few test orders before launch. A soft launch at one store for two weeks will expose problems cheaply.

## Pickup and Google: free local listings and local inventory ads

Google Merchant Center lets retailers show which products are in stock at their physical stores through free local listings and local inventory ads, with pickup options such as "pickup today" and "pickup later" where available. Google lists India among the countries for free local listings. Setting this up requires a Merchant Center account linked to your Google Business Profile, a local inventory feed with store-level availability, and accurate store data, which is why accurate store stock on your website comes first. Availability of specific pickup features can vary by country and account, so check the add-ons offered in your own Merchant Center account before planning a campaign around them. Our guide to Meta catalog ads and product feeds explains feed quality, which matters just as much for Google.

## Policies to publish

Add a short pickup section to your shipping or delivery policy page, and link it from checkout:

- Which stores offer pickup and their pickup hours.
- How customers are notified, and what they must bring.
- How long orders are held, and what happens if not collected.
- Whether someone else can collect on the customer's behalf, and how.
- How returns work for collected items: at any store or only the original store.

Keep the wording consistent with your returns and refunds policy. If you offer "pay at store", say so explicitly and explain cancellation.

## What it costs and how long it takes

Indicative ranges for a Pune retailer (not a quote):

- **Shopify with stores on Shopify POS:** enabling pickup, store pages, theme adjustments for product-page availability and notification templates often takes one to three weeks of work and might cost roughly ₹20,000 to ₹80,000, depending on the number of stores and theme changes.
- **WooCommerce:** enabling Local Pickup is quick; adding per-store stock with an inventory plugin, store pages and a locator might cost roughly ₹40,000 to ₹1,50,000.
- **Integration with an existing billing or POS system:** the biggest variable. If the POS has a usable API, a stock sync might be a few weeks of development; if it does not, it can be a larger project. Ranges from about ₹75,000 to ₹3,00,000 or more are realistic.
- **WhatsApp notifications:** template approval and integration, plus per-message charges from Meta.

The time-consuming part is usually cleaning product data so the same item has the same code online and in store. Budget for that.

## A launch checklist

- Every store has a page, a matching Google Business Profile and LocalBusiness markup.
- Store-level stock is accurate and syncs often enough, with a low-stock buffer.
- Product pages show pickup availability without slowing the page.
- Checkout offers Delivery or Pickup clearly, with no address fields for pickup.
- "Ready for pickup" is only sent when the item is actually ready.
- Staff know how to receive, pack, store, verify and hand over orders.
- The pickup policy is published and linked from checkout.
- You have tested an order end to end at each store, including cancellation and refund.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is click and collect in ecommerce?

Click and collect means customers buy or reserve a product on your website and pick it up from your physical store instead of having it delivered. The website shows which stores have stock, lets the customer choose pickup and a store at checkout, and sends a message when the order is ready.

### Does Shopify support store pickup in India?

Yes. Shopify's local pickup is enabled per location in the shipping and delivery settings. You set the expected pickup time and instructions, and staff mark orders ready for pickup and picked up. Customers only see pickup locations in their own country, so Indian stores can offer pickup to Indian customers.

### Can WooCommerce show different pickup locations?

Yes. The Local Pickup feature in WooCommerce's Checkout block lets you add several pickup locations with addresses and collection details. It does not check stock per store by default, so for store-level availability you need an inventory plugin or custom development.

### How do I show which store has stock on my website?

You need store-level inventory in your ecommerce platform, either tracked there directly (for example with Shopify POS) or synced from your billing system. The product page then shows availability per store, ideally with a small buffer so the last unit is not sold twice.

### Should click and collect be free?

Most retailers make pickup free because it saves delivery costs and brings customers into the store. Some charge a small fee for special handling or large items. Whatever you choose, show it clearly at checkout and in your delivery policy.
